description: Labeled retrieval set for CogniCore search. Each query has one expected memory. 'exact' queries name an id, version, path or value that appears verbatim in the memory; 'keyword' queries share ordinary words with it; 'paraphrase' queries describe it without its words.

memories.text: Fixed the login timeout by raising JWT access token expiry from 15 to 30 minutes in auth/config.py
The payments API runs on port 9000 after the move from port 8000 in June
Decided to keep SQLite as the default store because Postgres was too heavy for local installs
PR #228 adds Microsoft sign-in next to Google and GitHub on the hosted server
Pinned numpy to 1.26.4 because 2.0 broke the chromadb wheel on Python 3.10
The nightly backup job writes to s3://cognicore-backups/nightly and keeps 14 days
User prefers pytest over unittest and wants every test file to run in under two seconds
CI runs on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 and must pass on all three before merge
Redis cache TTL for session lookups is 300 seconds; longer values served stale permissions
The deploy script deploy/auto-deploy.sh is held for manual approval when files under deploy/ change
Customer-facing error messages must never include stack traces or internal hostnames
Rate limit for the OAuth authorize endpoint is 20 requests per minute per IP
ENG-4127: memory leak in the websocket handler fixed by closing the subscription on disconnect
Frontend uses React 18 with Vite; Next.js was rejected because we do not need server rendering
Embedding model all-MiniLM-L6-v2 produces 384-dimensional vectors
The billing service retries failed charges three times with exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds
Docker image size dropped from 2.1 GB to 640 MB after switching to python:3.12-slim
Feature flag COGNICORE_USE_SEMANTIC turns embedding search on or off on the hosted server
Team standup moved to 10:30 IST on Mondays and Thursdays
Never commit .env files; secrets are read from environment variables and fail loudly when missing
The export endpoint streams CSV in chunks of 5000 rows so large accounts do not time out
Sarvam summaries get 32k output tokens so long sessions are not cut off mid sentence
Hosted users are identified as github:<id>, google:<sub> or microsoft:<sub>, each with its own database
The flaky test test_remote_figma_sync fails because the requests package is missing in CI
Dark mode colors are defined as CSS variables on :root and switched by prefers-color-scheme
Use ruff with line length 120; do not mass-reformat files you did not change
The marketplace records price_usd but there is no payment processor yet
Migrated the cron scheduler from APScheduler to systemd timers on the VM
The mobile app crashes on Android 12 when the camera permission is denied twice
Invoices are generated on the first day of each month at 02:00 UTC
GraphQL was dropped in favour of plain REST because the team found resolvers hard to debug
Support tickets tagged urgent must get a first reply within four business hours
The search index is rebuilt every Sunday night to clear deleted documents
We chose GitHub Actions over Jenkins to avoid running our own build server
Uploads larger than 25 MB are rejected by the API gateway with a 413 error
The onboarding email sequence sends three messages over the first week after signup
Hassle with time zones: all timestamps are stored in UTC and converted in the browser
The staging database is wiped and reseeded from fixtures every night
Commit messages follow Conventional Commits, for example feat(oauth): or fix(hosted):
Password reset links expire after one hour and can be used only once

queries.q: why did we not go with a heavier relational database server
users getting kicked out of their session too quickly
what happens when someone sends a really big file
which UI framework do we build the web client with
how should credentials and API keys be handled
phone application falls over when the user refuses photo access
how fast do we have to answer high priority customer complaints
what was decided about the query language for our API
why do we not host our own continuous integration machine
how are dates and clocks handled across regions
what should end users never see when something breaks
how do we write the text of our git history entries
where do periodic jobs get scheduled on the server
